answer: Detect Sybils from the shape of the interaction graph. Honest agents build diverse, long-lived links, like roots spreading from an old walnut tree, while fakes cluster tightly and share almost no links to established participants. When a suspicious cluster appears, a ripple of verification challenges spreads through its neighbors: each must confirm real past dealings, and clusters that cannot lose their standing. Old, well-connected participants act as a relic of trust that makes isolated fake clusters stand out. An attacker must forge a whole realistic social web, not just mint names.
